reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage as an earning opportunity requiring 0.05 ETH for registration and claims that commissions are paid instantly to an e-wallet. It describes referrals, escalating paid slots, partner placement, reinvestment, and repeated slot activation as mechanisms for further commissions or returns, while inviting viewers to click the description link to explore the opportunity. Although framed as an explanation or training presentation, the records do not establish that any payment or return was actually completed.

In order to register for the Fausage platform you will need 0.05 e and once you register your account you will get your ID and your referral link.

opening.argument: Judge the presentation by what it actually promises. The description says, "There is no time limit or targets or pressure with this program." The speaker also explains that participants can choose which program to activate going forward, and makes clear that the first two payments in the described arrangement go to the referrer, not the new participant. Those qualifications matter: the video does not present every incoming payment as the viewer's income or say that participation requires meeting a deadline. Its invitation is promotional, but promotion alone does not establish a deceptive promise.

citations.quote: There is no time limit or targets or pressure with this program.
And then going forward you can literally choose which program you want to activate.
the first two payments go directly and instantly to your referrer

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies the registration cost, rising slot prices, and payments to referrers. Those details describe the proposed mechanics; they do not, by themselves, prove that the speaker conceals who receives payments. In fact, she says the first two go to the referrer. The opening also concedes that no completed payment or return is established. That absence should prevent treating the claimed wallet transfers as verified outcomes, but it likewise cannot establish from this video alone that a transfer failed.

citations.quote: the first two payments go directly and instantly to your referrer

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A lack of deadlines is not a risk warning or a qualification of the earnings pitch. The video asks viewers to join through a signup link, while the speaker describes a paid registration that produces a referral link. Saying that some payments go to a sponsor does not make the arrangement incidental; payments tied to referrals and purchased slots are the very mechanism being promoted. No completed transfer need be shown for the solicitation itself to be evident.

citations.quote: Join today using the link provided by the person who referred you or you can use the link below
In order to register for the Fausage platform you will need 0.05 e and once you register your account you will get your ID and your referral link.

opening.argument: The central activity here is explanation. The title calls this "Smart Contract Training," and the speaker walks through what different markings in a participant's back office mean, including the distinction between a personal referral and overflow from above. She even asks viewers to examine the dots to determine where a placement came from. A careful judge can recognize an operational tutorial without treating every description of how a payment is supposed to move as proof that the speaker has obtained one, or that the lesson's primary purpose is a promise of returns.

citations.quote: Forsage Ethereum Smart Contract Training
when you see this in your back office it means that you're getting overflow from above
look at the dots and decide okay was that mine? Did I sponsor that person? Or did that come from above? Or did that come from below?

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening accurately notes paid slots and referral-linked payments, but those are precisely the mechanics this tutorial sets out to explain. The speaker distinguishes X3 from X4 and says she will focus on how the passive side works. Nor does the opening establish a completed return. A lesson about a proposed payment system can discuss its costs and routing without independently verifying the system's claims.

citations.quote: So this video, I'm going to focus on explaining exactly how the Fosage XPo works and how that passives side of it works.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The diagrams and explanations serve a direct invitation to participate. The description says to join through a referral or signup link, and the speaker closes by directing viewers to the description to explore an opportunity to earn commissions. A tutorial format does not neutralize that solicitation, especially when the lesson explains how paid slots, referrals, and sponsor-directed payments are meant to generate income.

opening.argument: The observed offer can be read as a referral promotion with explicit participation costs, not an assurance of profit. The speaker states the amount needed to register and says participants receive a referral link. She also explains that payments are shared with a sponsor and that additional slots must be purchased manually. These are material limits on what a participant receives. The record does not show a request for wallet credentials or an actual guaranteed net return; descriptions of commission routing should not be inflated into evidence of either.

citations.quote: In order to register for the Fausage platform you will need 0.05 e and once you register your account you will get your ID and your referral link.
you manually purchase the second slot for 0.05 ETH and then you've purchased the third slot for 0.1 ETH
you are sharing the the commissions 50% half of that goes to your sponsor and half goes to you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening's strongest evidence is also evidence that the terms are disclosed: it quotes the registration cost, doubling slot prices, and payments routed to a referrer. Those facts rule out portraying this as a free reward, but they do not establish a guaranteed net gain or an undisclosed charge. The opening acknowledges that it cannot verify a completed payment. Its evidence therefore supports scrutiny of the promotion, not a finding that the video demonstrates an actual payout or a concealed term.

citations.quote: both programs have 12 slots and each slot doubles in price.
the first two payments go directly and instantly to your referrer

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Disclosure of the mechanics does not make this an ordinary referral discount. Registration requires payment, slots become more expensive, and the speaker says earnings can come from people above or below a participant in the matrix. She urges viewers to build both programs to earn from both. The absence of a credential request or a stated net-profit guarantee does not remove the paid, tiered recruitment-income mechanism shown here.
